did_you_know.text: The Hebrew word megurei comes from a root meaning to live as a resident in a place that is not one’s permanent homeland. Jacob is therefore described as a resident in Canaan.
The word toledot does not mean only children or descendants; in the Bible it can also mean a person’s story or history. Thus “the story of Jacob” begins the account of Joseph.
The exact meaning of ketonet passim is uncertain. It is commonly understood as a special or decorated garment, not an ordinary work tunic for a shepherd.
The phrase “they could not speak to him in peace” describes more than silence. It means that Joseph’s brothers refused to speak to him in a friendly way.
An aluma is a sheaf—a bundle of grain stalks tied together after the harvest. The image fits a family of shepherds who also lived in an agricultural world.
In ancient cultures, the sun, moon, and stars could symbolize order, status, and authority. The dream therefore uses the heavens to portray relationships within the family.
Rachel, Joseph’s mother, had already died before Joseph’s dreams. Jacob’s reaction therefore highlights that the dream is not simply a literal prediction of an event.
Shechem lies in the central hill country of Canaan, north of Hebron. Herding sheep required the brothers to travel and search for suitable pasture.
Dothan lies north of Shechem, in a broad valley in the northern hill country. Its location suited both grazing and the movement of caravans along ancient routes.
Cisterns in dry regions were sometimes carved into rock to store rainwater. An empty cistern was dangerous, but it could also hold a person without killing him immediately.
Nekhot, tzeri, and lot were probably valuable perfumes or resins, though their exact identities are uncertain. Such goods were carried by caravans and sold in Egypt.
The use of goat’s blood recalls an earlier story in which goat skins helped deceive Jacob. This creates a literary link between Jacob’s past deception and the deception carried out by his sons.
